focus.jbig: Amazon & Intel deepen the tech rout · AI reckoning intensifies · oil tops $103 · 8 setups boarded
focus.jtag: A second night of disappointing mega-cap earnings — Amazon light, Intel's Q4 guidance a disaster — pushed Nasdaq-100 futures down ~2.4% and S&P futures ~1%, extending the AI-capex selloff Alphabet triggered. The scanner boarded SYK, EXC, ORLY, COIN, VRT, XEL, ILMN (Type A) and IBB (Type C)
focus.jnote: The AI trade just took a second body blow. The S&P 500 fell 0.30% to 7,720.39 Thursday, snapping a three-day winning streak, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.38% to 26,184.72. Then the after-hours prints landed: Nasdaq-100 futures sank ~2.4% as earnings from Amazon and Intel raised fresh capex concerns — Amazon slumped ~7% and Intel plunged ~26% in premarket trading. Dow futures rose ~0.1% while S&P 500 futures dropped ~1%, a classic value-over-tech rotation. Oil kept climbing: WTI rose to ~$103 on Friday, up ~0.9%, while Brent rose to ~$113, up ~2.4%. The Magnificent 7 have collectively shed ~$4.0T in market value, with four constituents in bear-market territory. This is a live, two-night AI-earnings whipsaw with an oil tail on top — not a clean premium-selling backdrop.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the cleanest fundamentals are EXC and ORLY. Exelon double-beat (EPS +8.7%, revenue +7.8%) and gapped ~+2.5% — a defensive utility that tends to hold up on a risk-off tech-selloff morning. O’Reilly beat but revenue was essentially in line (+0.2%), gapping ~+3.9%. Both are bullish, but every Type A name printed on near-zero relative volume (0.00–0.06x), so the moves lack participation confirmation. On the breakout side, IBB (Type C, Grade B) is the one name that boarded on real volume (~1.8x), but it’s a same-day breakout into a risk-off tape. Watch-only on a RED day.
focus.notup: Three bearish Type A names boarded — SYK, COIN and VRT. Stryker posted a slight EPS miss and cut its 2026 guidance and gapped ~−10%; Coinbase sharply beat on EPS but revenue was flat and the stock fell after hours; Vertiv crushed estimates and raised guidance yet sold off on customer-concentration and valuation scrutiny. Selling bear calls into a two-night AI whipsaw with the VIX popping to ~18.4 invites a squeeze on any relief headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? P(≥1% gap) at ~42% is above the 35% trigger — that alone locks out GREEN — and composite ~63 is deep in WARM. On top of the math, this is a second consecutive night of violent mega-cap gaps (Intel ~−25%, Amazon ~−7%) that shows how unforgiving the AI-capex tape is right now, with an oil tail (WTI >$100) compounding it. Every boarded Type A name printed on near-zero volume, and the lone breakout is a same-day, unproven one. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the rout and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

The stock is indicated down hard — ~$281 premarket, off ~9.7% from the $311.75 close — a realized gap (~−11%) well past the 7.2% implied move. Scanner caveats: relative volume 0.01x gives no participation confirmation, open interest wasn’t returned, and 3 S/R layers sit just overhead ($280–$292). Watch-only on a RED day. Next earnings ~Jan 28, 2027.

Yet the stock is now fading: indicated ~$230 premarket, off ~6.5% from the $245.92 close (realized gap ~−6.2% vs the ~8.6% implied move), as the market frets about customer concentration, valuation, and its decision to stop disclosing order growth. Next earnings ~Feb 10, 2027.

Scanner caveats: it’s a same-day breakout — still proving itself, size accordingly — and it’s breaking out into a risk-off, Nasdaq ~−2.4% tape, exactly the backdrop where breakouts can fail. As an ETF there’s no single-name earnings gate, but verify the holdings’ earnings calendar. Watch-only on a RED day.

scenarios.label: Bad case — Broad derate deepens
scenarios.sub: The selloff spreads beyond tech or oil re-spikes; equities gap down broadly, VIX pushes into the low 20s, credit spreads widen

scenarios.label: Good case — Stabilization / dip-buy

scenarios.label: Tail — Hormuz shock / wider war
scenarios.sub: A Gulf shipping incident or escalation sends oil spiking hard on top of the tech selloff; a sharp VIX blow-off across risk assets

risks: The AI-capex narrative — two straight nights of mega-cap gaps (Alphabet, then Amazon ~−7% and Intel ~−25%) show the market is no longer rewarding heavy AI spending without evidence it generates sustainable profit. Any further soft tech read can re-crack the whole index — keep every spread clear of its name’s print.

Oil & the supply tail — WTI rose to ~$103 on Friday and Brent to ~$113, up ~2.4%; a Middle East escalation or Hormuz incident is the week’s biggest open-ended tail, and higher oil feeds inflation fear.

Flight to safety in bonds — the 10-year yield slid toward 4.9%, a seven-week low, as the tech/AI selloff pushed investors into government bonds. A sharp further risk-off move would pressure equities even as yields fall.

Near-zero volume on every Type A name — all seven post-earnings gaps printed on 0.00–0.06x relative volume, far below the 1.3x bar, so none has participation confirmation; treat all as watch-only until the open proves them.

Fed-path uncertainty — after the October hold, Chair Warsh left December open without clearly justifying the wait; stronger growth and firmer inflation data keep a December move live, able to whipsaw rates and risk.
